_description: CEDAR-PKD content data: modules and questions for the Adaptive Learning Engine prototype.

module.title: string — display title
module.topic_area: string — one of: kidney_basics | adpkd_diagnosis | adpkd_genetics
module.learning_objectives: array of strings — one per objective, written as 'Student will be able to...'
module.prerequisite_module_ids: array of module id strings — empty if no prerequisites
module.estimated_time_minutes: int — estimated time to complete module including questions

question.options: object — keys A/B/C/D, values are answer text strings
question.explanation: string — feedback shown after answering (correct or incorrect)
question.difficulty_prior: float 0.0-1.0 — hand-assigned prior (low=easy, high=hard); seeded into 2PL IRT model

demographic_tags.sex_specific: bool — true if content differs by sex/gender
demographic_tags.disease_stage_relevant: array of ints 1-5 — CKD stages where this question is especially relevant; empty = all stages
demographic_tags.family_planning_relevant: bool — true if content relates to family planning / reproductive decisions

question.distractor_misconceptions: object — keys match wrong option keys (e.g. 'B'), values are short misconception labels

modules.title: An Overview of ADPKD
learning_objectives: Define ADPKD and describe its prevalence (~1 in 1,000 lifetime risk)
Identify the primary genes associated with ADPKD (PKD1, PKD2 and five additional genes)
Describe the major complications of ADPKD beyond kidney failure
Explain why early diagnosis and genetic testing matter for ADPKD management
Distinguish ADPKD from other cystic kidney diseases

modules.title: ADPKD Genetics
learning_objectives: Explain autosomal dominant inheritance and the 50% transmission risk
Name all seven ADPKD-associated genes and their relative frequency
Describe what a pathogenic variant means in the context of ADPKD
Explain the difference between PKD1 and PKD2 in terms of disease severity
Recognize that de novo variants account for a minority of ADPKD cases

modules.title: Genetic Testing for ADPKD
learning_objectives: Identify clinical indications for ADPKD genetic testing
Explain what a genetic test report includes and how variants are classified
Describe implications of genetic testing for family members
Understand reproductive options available to individuals with ADPKD
Recognize barriers to genetic testing utilization and how to address them
Apply variant classification categories (pathogenic, likely pathogenic, VUS, etc.) to clinical scenarios

questions.text: Approximately how common is ADPKD in the general population?

options.A: 1 in 100 people
options.B: 1 in 1,000 people
options.C: 1 in 10,000 people
options.D: 1 in 100,000 people

questions.explanation: ADPKD affects approximately 1 in 1,000 people, making it one of the most common inherited kidney diseases worldwide. It is the fourth leading cause of end-stage renal disease.

distractor_misconceptions.A: ADPKD is rarer than a 1-in-100 condition like hypertension
distractor_misconceptions.C: ADPKD is more common than ultra-rare diseases; 1 in 10,000 understates its public health burden
distractor_misconceptions.D: ADPKD is not an ultra-rare disease; underestimating prevalence reduces urgency for screening

questions.text: ADPKD is caused by pathogenic variants in which two primary genes?

options.A: PKD1 and PKD2
options.B: BRCA1 and BRCA2
options.C: PKD1 and GANAB
options.D: PKD2 and ALG9

questions.explanation: The two primary ADPKD genes are PKD1 (~78% of cases) and PKD2 (~15% of cases). Five additional genes — GANAB, DNAJB11, ALG5, ALG9, and IFT140 — account for a smaller proportion of cases.

distractor_misconceptions.B: Confusing ADPKD with hereditary breast/ovarian cancer syndrome
distractor_misconceptions.C: GANAB is a minor ADPKD gene, not a primary one alongside PKD1
distractor_misconceptions.D: ALG9 is a minor ADPKD gene; conflating minor and major genes

questions.text: Beyond kidney disease, which of the following is a recognized complication of ADPKD?

options.A: Increased risk of lung cancer
options.B: Early-onset type 2 diabetes
options.C: Intracranial (brain) aneurysms
options.D: Progressive hearing loss

questions.explanation: ADPKD is a systemic disease. Intracranial aneurysms occur in ~8% of ADPKD patients (higher than the general population) and are a cause of hemorrhagic stroke. Cystic liver disease and cardiac valve abnormalities are also recognized extra-renal complications.

distractor_misconceptions.A: ADPKD does not increase lung cancer risk; confusing multisystem disease with oncologic conditions
distractor_misconceptions.B: Type 2 diabetes is not a feature of ADPKD; confusing metabolic with genetic kidney disease
distractor_misconceptions.D: Hearing loss is associated with Alport syndrome, not ADPKD; confusing inherited kidney diseases

questions.text: Research shows that delayed ADPKD diagnosis is associated with which outcome?

options.A: Faster cyst growth but no change in survival
options.B: Reduced eligibility for tolvaptan treatment
options.C: Greater likelihood of requiring dialysis before age 40
options.D: Increased all-cause mortality

questions.explanation: Preliminary data from a cohort of 12,217 veterans with ADPKD showed that diagnostic delays greater than 10 years were associated with significantly increased all-cause mortality (HR 1.14, p=0.015), even after adjusting for age and kidney function. This underscores the urgency of early, accurate diagnosis.

distractor_misconceptions.A: Believing that diagnosis timing only affects cyst biology, not survival
distractor_misconceptions.B: Tolvaptan eligibility is based on disease progression rate, not diagnosis timing per se
distractor_misconceptions.C: While serious, early dialysis is not the primary mortality driver associated with diagnostic delay in the evidence

questions.text: Which of the following best describes why ADPKD affects kidney function over time?

options.A: The kidneys become inflamed and scarred due to repeated infections
options.B: Fluid-filled cysts grow progressively, replacing normal kidney tissue and reducing function
options.C: The immune system attacks kidney cells, reducing their ability to filter blood
options.D: Calcium deposits block the kidney tubules, preventing urine formation

questions.explanation: In ADPKD, mutations in PKD1 or PKD2 cause abnormal cell signaling that leads to cyst formation. Cysts grow over decades, physically compressing and replacing functional kidney tissue, ultimately reducing the kidney's ability to filter waste from the blood.

distractor_misconceptions.A: Confusing ADPKD with chronic pyelonephritis or reflux nephropathy
distractor_misconceptions.C: Confusing ADPKD with autoimmune kidney diseases like lupus nephritis
distractor_misconceptions.D: Confusing ADPKD with nephrocalcinosis or obstructive uropathy

questions.text: A patient with ADPKD asks if their children will definitely develop the disease. What is the most accurate response?

options.A: Yes, all children of an ADPKD patient will inherit the condition
options.B: No, ADPKD skips generations so children are typically unaffected
options.C: Each child has a 50% chance of inheriting the pathogenic variant
options.D: Only male children are at risk of inheriting ADPKD

questions.explanation: ADPKD follows autosomal dominant inheritance. Each pregnancy has a 50% probability of inheriting the pathogenic variant, regardless of sex. It does not skip generations — an affected parent has a 50/50 chance of passing it on with each child.

distractor_misconceptions.A: Believing autosomal dominant means 100% transmission rather than 50%
distractor_misconceptions.B: Confusing autosomal dominant with recessive inheritance patterns that can skip generations
distractor_misconceptions.D: Confusing autosomal dominant with X-linked inheritance

questions.text: In autosomal dominant inheritance, what does 'dominant' mean?

options.A: Only one copy of the pathogenic variant is needed to cause the disease
options.B: Both copies of the gene must carry the variant for disease to occur
options.C: The variant is located on the dominant X chromosome
options.D: The disease is more severe in dominant individuals in the family

questions.explanation: Dominant means that a single pathogenic variant in one copy of the gene is sufficient to cause disease. This contrasts with recessive conditions (like autosomal recessive PKD) where two pathogenic variants — one in each copy — are required.

distractor_misconceptions.B: Confusing autosomal dominant with autosomal recessive inheritance
distractor_misconceptions.C: Confusing 'dominant' in genetics with chromosomal location
distractor_misconceptions.D: Misinterpreting 'dominant' as a social or clinical hierarchy term

questions.text: Which ADPKD gene is associated with more severe disease and earlier onset of kidney failure?

options.A: PKD1
options.B: PKD2
options.C: GANAB
options.D: IFT140

questions.explanation: PKD1 variants generally produce a more severe phenotype, with median age of ESRD around 58 years versus ~79 years for PKD2 variants. This genotype-phenotype correlation has clinical implications for risk stratification and treatment decisions.

distractor_misconceptions.C: GANAB variants cause a milder, predominantly hepatic cystic phenotype
distractor_misconceptions.D: IFT140 is associated with a milder phenotype often with extra-renal features

questions.text: If a patient has ADPKD but neither parent has the disease, what is the most likely explanation?

options.A: The patient actually has autosomal recessive PKD, not ADPKD
options.B: The patient has a de novo (new) pathogenic variant that was not inherited from either parent
options.C: One parent must be a carrier but shows no symptoms due to incomplete penetrance
options.D: Environmental factors caused the patient to develop ADPKD without a genetic cause

questions.explanation: De novo variants — new mutations arising for the first time in the patient rather than being inherited — account for approximately 5-10% of ADPKD cases. This explains cases where neither parent is affected. ADPKD has essentially complete penetrance, so an affected parent would typically show symptoms.

distractor_misconceptions.A: Assuming negative family history rules out ADPKD rather than de novo variants
distractor_misconceptions.C: ADPKD has near-complete penetrance; incomplete penetrance is not the primary explanation
distractor_misconceptions.D: Believing environmental exposures alone can cause ADPKD without genetic variants

questions.text: Which of the following is true about the seven genes associated with ADPKD?

options.A: All seven genes produce equally severe disease
options.B: Variants in GANAB and DNAJB11 are the most common cause of ADPKD
options.C: Only PKD1 and PKD2 have been validated as ADPKD genes; the others are under investigation
options.D: PKD1 and PKD2 account for the large majority of cases; the remaining five genes are less common

questions.explanation: PKD1 accounts for ~78% and PKD2 for ~15% of ADPKD cases. GANAB, DNAJB11, ALG5, ALG9, and IFT140 are validated ADPKD genes but account for a minority of cases and are often associated with milder or atypical presentations.

distractor_misconceptions.A: Assuming all ADPKD genes produce the same severity
distractor_misconceptions.B: Overestimating the frequency of minor ADPKD genes
distractor_misconceptions.C: Underestimating the current evidence base for the five additional ADPKD genes

questions.text: A patient with ADPKD and a PKD2 variant asks how their prognosis compares to a friend who has a PKD1 variant. What is the most accurate statement?

options.A: Their prognosis is identical — gene type does not affect ADPKD outcomes
options.B: They will progress faster because PKD2 variants cause more rapid cyst growth
options.C: They will likely have a slower disease course, with later onset of kidney failure than their friend
options.D: Both genes have the same kidney outcomes, but PKD2 is associated with worse liver disease

questions.explanation: PKD2 variants are associated with a milder disease course, with median ESRD around age 79 compared to ~58 for PKD1. This genotype-phenotype information is directly relevant to clinical counseling and treatment decisions such as tolvaptan eligibility.

distractor_misconceptions.A: Believing gene type has no prognostic significance for ADPKD
distractor_misconceptions.D: Confusing hepatic cystic disease severity between PKD1 and PKD2

questions.text: Why is genetic testing important even for patients who already have an imaging-based ADPKD diagnosis?

options.A: Genetic testing can reverse the diagnosis if imaging was incorrect
options.B: Knowing the specific gene and variant helps with prognosis, treatment decisions, and family planning
options.C: Genetic testing is required by law before prescribing tolvaptan
options.D: Imaging cannot distinguish ADPKD from other cystic kidney diseases, so genetic testing is always needed first

questions.explanation: Even with an established imaging diagnosis, genetic testing adds value by identifying the specific gene (PKD1 vs PKD2 affects prognosis), the variant class (pathogenic vs VUS affects confidence), informing tolvaptan eligibility, enabling cascade testing of family members, and supporting reproductive decision-making.

distractor_misconceptions.A: Thinking genetic testing is only useful for confirming or reversing an uncertain diagnosis
distractor_misconceptions.C: Overstating legal requirements; tolvaptan eligibility is based on clinical criteria, not genetic testing mandate
distractor_misconceptions.D: Overstating imaging ambiguity; imaging can diagnose ADPKD but genetic testing adds layered value

questions.text: Which of the following patients has the strongest indication for ADPKD genetic testing?

options.A: A 70-year-old with bilateral kidney cysts and no family history
options.B: A patient with unilateral cysts found incidentally during abdominal imaging
options.C: A 28-year-old considering pregnancy whose parent has ADPKD but imaging is inconclusive
options.D: A patient with ESRD already on dialysis with no genetic testing interest

questions.explanation: Genetic testing is most impactful when results will change clinical management. A young patient considering pregnancy whose parent has ADPKD has the highest stakes: confirming or ruling out the familial variant has direct implications for their own care, prenatal testing, and preimplantation genetic diagnosis options.

distractor_misconceptions.A: Simple cysts are common in older adults and do not necessarily indicate ADPKD
distractor_misconceptions.B: Unilateral incidental cysts have many benign causes and do not strongly indicate ADPKD
distractor_misconceptions.D: At ESRD, genetic testing has less immediate impact on clinical management

questions.text: A genetic test report returns a result of 'Variant of Uncertain Significance (VUS)' in PKD1. What does this mean for the patient?

options.A: The variant is definitely causing the patient's ADPKD
options.B: There is not yet enough evidence to classify the variant as pathogenic or benign
options.C: The variant is benign and can be ignored clinically
options.D: The patient should immediately start tolvaptan because all PKD1 variants are pathogenic

questions.explanation: A VUS means the laboratory has insufficient evidence to classify the variant as either disease-causing or benign. VUSes should not be used to make clinical decisions. They may be reclassified as more evidence accumulates, so patients and families should be re-contacted if reclassification occurs.

distractor_misconceptions.A: Treating a VUS as equivalent to a pathogenic variant
distractor_misconceptions.C: Treating a VUS as benign and dismissing it
distractor_misconceptions.D: Using variant presence alone to justify treatment without pathogenicity confirmation

questions.text: A patient with confirmed ADPKD (PKD1 pathogenic variant) has two adult siblings who have never been tested. What is the recommended approach?

options.A: Siblings do not need testing unless they develop symptoms
options.B: Siblings should have imaging only; genetic testing is not useful for cascade testing
options.C: Only female siblings should be tested due to higher ADPKD risk in women
options.D: Cascade genetic testing should be offered to all first-degree relatives who wish to know their status

questions.explanation: Cascade genetic testing — offering targeted testing for the known familial variant to at-risk relatives — is a key benefit of ADPKD genetic testing. Each sibling has a 50% probability of carrying the variant. Early identification allows pre-symptomatic monitoring, lifestyle modifications, and informed reproductive planning.

distractor_misconceptions.A: Waiting for symptoms before testing misses the opportunity for early intervention
distractor_misconceptions.B: Targeted variant testing is efficient and actionable for cascade testing; dismissing its value
distractor_misconceptions.C: ADPKD risk is equal for males and females (autosomal, not X-linked)

questions.text: Which of the following is a known barrier to genetic testing utilization among nephrologists, based on survey evidence?

options.A: Insufficient training in genetics and uncertainty about how to interpret test results
options.B: Lack of available genetic tests for ADPKD genes
options.C: Patient refusal of genetic testing in the majority of cases
options.D: Insurance covering genetic testing prevents ordering due to prior authorization burden

questions.explanation: Surveys of nephrologists show that over 50% report insufficient training in genetics, and that lower genetics education is associated with fewer genetic referrals. Nearly one-third of nephrologists report not using genetic testing despite clinical indications. Educational resources are consistently cited as a top unmet need.

distractor_misconceptions.B: Genetic tests for all seven ADPKD genes are commercially available
distractor_misconceptions.C: Patient acceptance of testing is generally higher than physician ordering rates
distractor_misconceptions.D: While insurance issues exist, the primary barrier identified in surveys is physician education

questions.text: A young woman with ADPKD wants to have children but does not want to pass the condition on. Which reproductive option can help achieve this?

options.A: Choosing adoption is the only way to avoid passing ADPKD to children
options.B: ADPKD is too unpredictable for reproductive planning to be useful
options.C: Preimplantation genetic testing (PGT) during IVF can identify embryos without the ADPKD variant
options.D: Prenatal testing can detect ADPKD but results cannot be used to change the pregnancy outcome

questions.explanation: Preimplantation genetic testing (PGT) involves genetic testing of embryos created through IVF before implantation. Embryos without the pathogenic variant can be selected for transfer, allowing the patient to have a biological child without ADPKD. Prenatal testing (CVS or amniocentesis) is also available for established pregnancies.

distractor_misconceptions.A: Unaware of reproductive genetic technologies that allow biological parenthood
distractor_misconceptions.B: Fatalism about ADPKD genetics limiting reproductive options
distractor_misconceptions.D: Misunderstanding the scope of prenatal genetic testing options

questions.text: How are variants in ADPKD genes typically classified on a genetic test report?

options.A: As either 'positive' or 'negative' with no further detail
options.B: Using a five-tier system: Pathogenic, Likely Pathogenic, Variant of Uncertain Significance, Likely Benign, or Benign
options.C: By severity score from 1–10 based on predicted protein damage
options.D: As 'high risk' or 'low risk' using a proprietary algorithm specific to each testing laboratory

questions.explanation: The ACMG-AMP guidelines provide a standardized five-tier classification: Pathogenic (P), Likely Pathogenic (LP), Variant of Uncertain Significance (VUS), Likely Benign (LB), and Benign (B). P and LP variants are considered clinically actionable; VUS should not drive clinical decisions; LB and B are not considered disease-causing.

distractor_misconceptions.A: Oversimplifying classification to a binary positive/negative result
distractor_misconceptions.C: Confusing ACMG-AMP classification with computational prediction scores like SIFT or PolyPhen
distractor_misconceptions.D: Believing variant classification is non-standardized and laboratory-specific

questions.text: A male patient with ADPKD is CKD Stage 4. He asks whether genetic testing is still useful at this stage. Which is most accurate?

options.A: Genetic testing is not useful at CKD Stage 4 because treatment options are limited
options.B: Genetic testing should be done urgently to qualify for tolvaptan before dialysis
options.C: Genetic testing will determine whether the patient needs a kidney transplant
options.D: Genetic testing can still benefit family members and inform transplant donor evaluation from relatives

questions.explanation: Even at advanced CKD, genetic testing provides value for cascade testing of at-risk relatives, informing living donor evaluation (a relative who carries the same variant may not be an appropriate kidney donor), and providing prognostic clarity. Tolvaptan is generally indicated for earlier-stage patients at risk of rapid progression.

distractor_misconceptions.A: Assuming advanced disease makes genetic testing irrelevant
distractor_misconceptions.B: Misunderstanding tolvaptan indication; it is for earlier-stage, rapidly progressing patients
distractor_misconceptions.C: Conflating genetic diagnosis with transplant listing decisions

questions.text: ADPKD disproportionately affects women in one specific complication. Which is it?

options.A: Liver cysts (polycystic liver disease) are more severe and symptomatic in women, especially those who have been pregnant or used oral contraceptives
options.B: Women with ADPKD progress to kidney failure significantly faster than men
options.C: Intracranial aneurysms occur exclusively in women with ADPKD
options.D: ADPKD-related hypertension is more common and severe in women

questions.explanation: Polycystic liver disease is a well-recognized sex-specific complication of ADPKD: women, particularly those with a history of pregnancy or exogenous estrogen use, develop larger and more symptomatic hepatic cysts. This is clinically important for counseling women with ADPKD considering pregnancy or hormonal contraception.

distractor_misconceptions.B: Men and women progress to kidney failure at similar rates overall (men may progress slightly faster)
distractor_misconceptions.C: Intracranial aneurysms affect both sexes with ADPKD; not exclusive to women
distractor_misconceptions.D: Hypertension is common in ADPKD in both sexes and typically appears before significant kidney decline
